scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Dal that takes an hour in a pot is done in a few whistles in a pressure cooker. What's the trick?

scenes.name: boil
scenes.text: In an open pot, water boils at about a hundred degrees. Extra heat just turns it to steam, the water can't get hotter.

scenes.name: seal
scenes.text: A pressure cooker locks shut with a rubber gasket. Steam can't escape, so the pressure inside rises.

scenes.name: hotter
scenes.text: Higher pressure raises the boiling point. At around one extra atmosphere, water boils at about a hundred and twenty degrees.

scenes.name: faster
scenes.text: That hotter water and steam push heat into the food much faster, so it softens in a fraction of the time.

scenes.name: whistle
scenes.text: The weight on top lifts when pressure gets high enough, and releases steam with a whistle. That keeps the pressure steady.

scenes.name: safety
scenes.text: If the vent gets blocked, a safety valve or plug releases the pressure. So keep the vent clean, and the gasket in good shape.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Seal, pressure, hotter water, whistle. Cooking with physics. Follow for more on how things really work.
